content: Linda Sloan is a Canadian politician currently serving as a municipal councillor in Edmonton, Alberta. She graduated from the Foothills Hospital School of Nursing in 1982 and began her career as a registered nurse. Early in her career, she became actively involved in the Staff Nurses Associations of Alberta, where she served as president from 1992 to 1997. She also participated in the National Federation of Nurses Unions and the Alberta Association of Registered Nurses. In 1997, Sloan ran for a seat in the Legislative Assembly of Alberta, representing the Edmonton Riverview riding as a candidate for the Liberal Party of Alberta. She won the election, defeating her closest competitor, Progressive Conservative Gwen Harris, by a margin of over 900 votes. During her tenure in the legislature, Sloan served as the Liberal opposition critic for social services, child welfare, and disability programs. In this role, she advocated for extending adoption rights to homosexual couples and introduced a private member's bill proposing the establishment of a children's advocate who would report directly to the legislature. When Liberal leader Grant Mitchell resigned in 1998, Sloan was one of four candidates who sought to succeed him. However, Nancy MacBeth won the leadership on the first ballot. Sloan chose not to run for re-election in 2001 and instead pursued a position on Edmonton's city council in 2004. She finished second out of nine candidates in Ward 1, behind incumbent councillor and former Liberal caucus colleague Karen Leibovici, and was elected to the council. As a city councillor, Sloan has been responsible for the Senior Citizens portfolio. She is married and has two children.
